_meta.why: Every downstream engine (Safe-to-Spend, emergency fund, forecasting, purchase advisor) depends on knowing which outflows are obligations and what each rupee became. AI-CLS needs seed knowledge to classify from day one, before it has learned from user corrections.
_meta.what: Seed knowledge for AI-CLS: (a) merchant->category rules for Indian merchants, (b) category defaults incl. default_nature, (c) stream-classification thresholds (§8.2), (d) the nature auto-classification order (§8.3.1), (e) the Stage-1 matching thresholds (§8.1). Precedence at runtime: user rule > learned model (>=0.85) > this knowledge base > 'Uncategorised' prompt.
_meta.result: A fresh install classifies Swiggy as Dining/WANT and BESCOM as Utilities/NEED with clearly-labelled 'estimate - improves with data' confidence.
changelog: 2026-07-17 — Created from SRS v1.7 §8.1, §8.2, §8.3; merchant list is a starter set, extended by user corrections.

2026-08-08 — Issue 4.1: every merchant_rules and category_defaults row gains a stable rule_id and its own version (AI-ARC-006), and category_defaults gains `key` — the id the seeded `category` row is derived from, so renaming a category in the editor never changes which row it is. category_defaults is now read by CategorySeed (:core:model); merchant_rules still has no runtime consumer — see ADR-0014.

2026-08-10 — Issue 4.2: merchant_rules gains its consumer (:domain:engines:classification) and this file gains `stage1` — the confidence a match is worth and the floor below which Stage 1 defers to the user instead of guessing. CLS-USER-HISTORY is the id the §8.1(a) correction-history tier cites; it names no merchant because the user's own past corrections are its rows. §8.1(c), the on-device TF-IDF + logistic model, is still unbuilt — see ADR-0015.

2026-08-10 — CLS-MER-011 -> v1.1: `coin` dropped from its alternatives. Read as a rule for the first time, it files any merchant with `coin` as a word — a laundromat, a coin dealer — under Investment. Zerodha's Coin is always described as `ZERODHA COIN` or `COIN BY ZERODHA`, both of which `zerodha` already matches, so nothing is lost. Found by the eval set in issue 4.2; the id is kept and the version bumped, never renamed (id_policy).
_meta.id_policy: rule_id is permanent. To retire a row set `enabled: false` — never rename or delete an id that may already be cited in a stored insight (AI-ARC-006).

stage1._algorithm: normalise the merchant, then: (a) if the user has categorised this exact merchant before, propose the category they used, worth 10000 * matching / total bps; (b) otherwise the first merchant_rules row whose token matches, worth exact_match_bps for a whole-string match and word_match_bps for a token inside a longer descriptor. Anything under min_confidence_bps, and any tie between two rules naming different categories, proposes nothing.
stage1._why_whole_word: CLS-MER-010 holds `lic`. Matched as a substring it files LICIOUS (a meat delivery service) under Insurance. A token match is not a refinement here, it is the difference between the rule working and the rule being wrong.

stream_classification._algorithm: score = 0.45*(1-min(cv,1)) + 0.35*(1-min(cadence,1)) + 0.20*dayLock, over last 6 months, n>=3 months activity

overrides.known_obligation_is_fixed: txns linked to loan EMIs, recurring rules, or insurance premia are FIXED regardless of score
overrides.cold_start: with < 2 months data, use category-level Indian priors labelled 'estimate - improves with data'

order.rule: txn on a loan account -> LIABILITY (principal = liability reduction; interest+fees = true cost)
transfer to an investment/goal-linked account -> INVESTMENT
creates/updates an asset record (gold, vehicle, property, holdings) -> ASSET
user rule from past corrections (merchant/category) -> learned nature
category default_nature from this knowledge base -> NEED or WANT
amount > 3x category median in a NEED category -> prompt once, remember

natures.NEED: Essential living costs. Counts in true spend; feeds emergency-fund essentials and the 50% band.
natures.WANT: Discretionary consumption. Counts in true spend; the 30% band; highest Purchase-Advisor scrutiny.
natures.INVESTMENT: Money that stays yours and grows. Excluded from spend; counts as saving rate; the 20% band.
natures.ASSET: Consumption converted to a lasting asset. Excluded from true spend; MUST create/update a linked asset record.
natures.LIABILITY: Debt service. Auto-split: principal = liability reduction; interest & fees = true cost, counted like NEED.

nature_classification.true_spend_formula: trueSpend = NEED + WANT + interest/fees (ASSET and INVESTMENT conversions shown separately)
nature_classification.low_confidence_handling: flagged for one-tap review in the weekly digest, never blocking save
